skill.name: create-issue
skill.description: Creates structured GitHub or Jira issues by detecting the active tracker, selecting an issue type, and applying task, bug, or story templates.
skill.summary: Create structured GitHub or Jira issues from a user request.
skill.author: Cloud-Officer

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown examples, inline command references, or issue template text, so I adjudicated them as false positives. Medium semantic risk remains from unescaped shell arguments and a fixed temporary file that may overwrite or delete workspace content.

remediation.issue: User-provided values can reach shell command arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Escape or validate title, label, assignee, summary, type, and priority values before command execution. Prefer structured argument passing when available.

remediation.issue: The workflow uses a fixed temporary filename.
remediation.suggestion: Create a unique temporary file outside the repository, or check for an existing issue-body.md before writing and deleting it.
Show the target tracker, title, labels, and assignee, then ask for confirmation before running the create command.

static_findings.snippet: If GitHub issues are enabled, use `gh issue create`.
Add `--assignee "<username>"` if user specified an assignee.
If GitHub issues are disabled, use `jira issue create`.
Add `--assignee "<username>"` if user specified an assignee.
- Always prefix summary with repo name: `[repo-name] Brief description`
- Always use `--no-input` flag to prevent interactive prompts
- Do NOT specify a project (`-p` or `--project`) - use default from user's config
- Use `##` for main headings, `-` for bullet points
- **Additional Context:** Provide any extra technical notes that could aid implementation
- **Blockers:** Identify potential blockers that might impact progress

semantic_findings.title: Unescaped User Input in Shell Command Arguments
semantic_findings.description: The skill asks the agent to place user-provided title, label, assignee, summary, and priority values into shell commands. Without explicit escaping or validation, a malicious value containing shell metacharacters could alter the command.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The shell command templates include user-derived placeholders such as title, label, assignee, and summary. The file does not include instructions to escape or validate those values before execution.

semantic_findings.title: Fixed Temporary File May Clobber Workspace Content
semantic_findings.description: The workflow always writes and deletes issue-body.md in the current workspace. If that file already exists, the workflow could overwrite or remove user data.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The skill explicitly names issue-body.md as the body file and later tells the agent to delete the temp file. There is no check for an existing file with the same name.

content.value_statement: Creating consistent tracker issues takes time and depends on each repository tracker setup. This skill detects GitHub issue availability, then prepares a GitHub or Jira issue with the right template.
actual_capabilities: Detects whether GitHub Issues are enabled through the GitHub CLI.
Creates GitHub issues with a title, body file, label, and optional assignee.
Creates Jira issues with type, priority, label, summary, template, and optional assignee.
Formats Task, Bug, and Story issue bodies from built-in templates.
Maps severity values to Jira priority names.
Prefixes Jira summaries with the repository name.
limitations: Requires authenticated GitHub CLI, Jira CLI, and Git access.
Relies on the user default Jira project configuration.
Does not validate tracker labels, usernames, or permissions before submission.
Uses a fixed issue-body.md temporary file unless the agent adapts the workflow.

use_cases.title: File a Production Bug
use_cases.description: Create a structured bug report with environment, impact, reproduction steps, workaround, and severity details.

use_cases.title: Plan a Feature Story
use_cases.description: Turn a feature request into a story with business value, design notes, API impact, risks, and acceptance criteria.

use_cases.title: Track Engineering Tasks
use_cases.description: Create implementation tasks with scope, security notes, testing details, and technical context for the repository.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Task
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a standard task.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a task issue for adding password reset emails. Include scope, testing details, and no security impact.

prompt_templates.title: Report a Bug
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request with severity and assignment.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a bug issue for checkout failing on Safari. Use high severity, include reproduction steps, and assign it to alex.

prompt_templates.title: Write a User Story
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a story for admin bulk user import. Include business value, API changes, testing strategy, and acceptance criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Route by Tracker
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request that relies on tracker detection.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create the right issue for this repository. If GitHub Issues are enabled, use GitHub. Otherwise, create a Jira story with medium severity.

output_examples.input: Create a bug for login timeouts in production with high severity.
output_examples.output: The skill creates a bug issue with environment, actual behavior, expected behavior, impact, workaround, and related information sections.

output_examples.input: Create a story for mobile onboarding improvements.
output_examples.output: The skill creates a story with user group, business value, design notes, API considerations, risks, testing strategy, and acceptance criteria.

output_examples.input: Create a task to update API documentation and assign it to priya.
output_examples.output: The skill creates a task issue with scope, security impact, testing details, technical notes, and the requested assignee.

best_practices: Review the generated title, body, label, and assignee before allowing the CLI command to run.
Configure GitHub, Jira, and repository authentication before invoking the skill.
Provide clear severity, environment, and reproduction details for bug reports.
anti_patterns: Do not pass shell metacharacters in titles, labels, summaries, or assignee values.
Do not run the workflow when an important issue-body.md file already exists.
Do not use it for projects where tracker permissions or defaults are unknown.

faq.question: Does this work with both GitHub and Jira?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks whether GitHub Issues are enabled and otherwise uses Jira.

faq.question: Does it create the issue automatically?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow is designed to run the configured CLI after preparing the issue body.

faq.question: What tools must be installed?
faq.answer: The GitHub CLI, Jira CLI, and Git must be installed and authenticated.

faq.question: Can it choose the issue type?
faq.answer: Yes. It selects Task, Bug, or Story from the user request.

faq.question: Can it assign users?
faq.answer: Yes. It adds an assignee when the request includes a supported username.

faq.question: Does it validate labels or projects?
faq.answer: No. It relies on tracker defaults, existing labels, and current user permissions.
